8.3.  Nonexistent Data

   A recursive resolver receives a query for the A record for
   "ipv6.toronto.redhat.ca".  It includes the CHAIN option with the
   following parameters:

   o  Option-code, set to 13

correct_text:
o  The upstream recursive resolver adds the CHAIN option to the DNS
      response as follows:

      *  Option-code, set to 13

      *  Option-length, set to 13

      *  The closest trust point is set to "example.com." (0x07 0x65 0x78 0x61 0x6d 0x70 0x6c 0x65 0x03 0x63 0x6f 0x6d 0x00)
notes:
The provided example seems inconsistent with: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7901#section-5.4
Specifically:
   If a CHAIN answer would be bigger than the recursive resolver is
   willing to serve, it SHOULD send a partial chain starting with the
   data closest to the top of the chain.  The client MAY resend the
   query with an updated closest trust point until it has received the full chain. 
   The CHAIN response will contain the lowest closest trust
   point that was included in the CHAIN answer.

I may be confusing the wording here or misunderstanding things, but I understood that the lowest closest trust point in the example response is "example.com." and not "com.". This is especially important to enable clients to use the CHAIN option value instead of checking records in the authority section.
